headline: GOLDEN TRIANGLE SYSTEM ALIVE: Goldstorm Drills 407.55m at Crown — 15m at 2.89 g/t AuEq on KSM Trend
snippet: Goldstorm Metals (TSXV: GSTM) released first assays from Phase I diamond drilling at its Crown property in British Columbia's Golden Triangle — hole OR-26-03 returned 407.55 metres of 0.39 g/t gold equivalent from 114.45 metres depth, including a higher-grade core of 15.0 metres at 2.89 g/t AuEq, on a trend corridor between the district-scale KSM and Treaty Creek deposits. Rock sampling at Crown has returned values up to 155 g/t gold from a gouge-filled shear zone; four of the seven Phase I holes remain pending assays, and the body is open in all directions.

headline: PENTAGON BACKS US RARE EARTH PLANT: Phoenix Tailings Picks Rochester for $375M — Part of $1.2B Freedom Project
snippet: Phoenix Tailings selected Eastman Business Park in Rochester, New York for its Freedom Separation facility — a $375 million rare earth processing plant backed by a conditional $500 million Pentagon debt commitment, forming part of a $1.2 billion rare earth midstream platform. The 500,000-square-foot plant will process more than 18,000 tons of mined and recycled feedstock annually and produce over 4,400 tons per year of separated rare earth oxides, with production ramping from 2027 and full output targeted for 2028.

headline: DRAGONFLY STEPS NORTH: K2 Gold Punches 83.82m at 3.40 g/t Au at Mojave — Widest, Richest Hole of 14,000m Program
snippet: K2 Gold (TSXV: KTO) released the final four holes from Phase I of its 14,000-metre program at the Dragonfly Zone, Mojave Project in California — the headline hole DF26-031 returned 83.82 metres at 3.40 g/t Au from surface, including 19.81 metres at 7.51 g/t Au, drilled as a 94-metre step-out north of K2's previous best intercept of 45.72m at 6.68 g/t. The Phase I campaign has completed 42 holes for 8,013 metres total; the program is fully funded and permitted for Phase II, which will test extensions along strike.

headline: OIL TRAPS GOLD AT $4,127: Brent Above $110 Revives Inflation Fears — Four-Day Slide Continues Into FOMC Week
snippet: Spot gold steadied at $4,127 per ounce on October 21, near a one-week low, as Brent crude holding above $110 per barrel stoked inflation expectations and dented the case for Federal Reserve rate cuts ahead of the October 27–28 FOMC. Analysts note the correction is macro-driven rather than fundamental — central bank demand and ETF inflows remain strong — but the oil-yield-dollar triangle needs to shift in gold's favour before the next leg upward resumes.

headline: FULL CONSOLIDATION: Cerro de Pasco Secures 100% of Quiulacocha Tailings in Peru — 90Mt Deposit Now Sole Owner
snippet: Cerro de Pasco Resources (CSE: CDPR) signed definitive agreements with AMSAC to acquire the remaining interest in the Quiulacocha tailings deposit in Peru, consolidating 100% ownership of the approximately 90-million-tonne polymetallic tailings pile and securing surface rights. The Quiulacocha tailings represent a large-scale silver-zinc-lead reprocessing opportunity in a historic Andean district; full surface rights control eliminates the key permitting and development overhang that had long deferred a timeline to production.

headline: NEVADA GOLD CONSOLIDATION: SSR Mining Pays $464M Cash for Roxmore's 5.2Moz Converse Project Next to Marigold
snippet: SSR Mining (TSX: SSRM) agreed to acquire Roxmore Resources in an all-cash deal at C$6.75 per share — approximately US$464 million — to gain control of the Converse gold project in Nevada, a 5.2-million-ounce resource (2.2Moz indicated + 3.0Moz inferred) located six kilometres from SSR's Marigold complex along the Battle Mountain-Eureka Trend. SSR expects Converse to add 150,000–170,000 ounces annually from 2033 with initial capital of US$800–900 million, partially offset by at least US$200 million in synergies from proximity to existing Marigold infrastructure.

headline: TIRIS ECONOMICS CONFIRMED: Aura Energy BFS Returns $500M NPV at $90/lb U3O8 — FID Target Set for December 2026
snippet: Aura Energy (ASX: AEE) released its bankable feasibility study for the Tiris uranium project in Mauritania, returning a post-tax NPV of US$500.3 million at US$90/lb with an IRR of 28% and a 3.2-year payback; development capital is US$349.8 million and AISC is US$41.25/lb across a 26-year mine life producing 46.1 million pounds U3O8. The company is targeting a final investment decision in December 2026, contingent on finalising a funding package that includes discussions with the US DFC for up to US$170 million in senior debt and a cornerstone equity stake from a strategic nuclear utility.

headline: TUMAS CLOCK STOPS: Deep Yellow Pulls Q4 FID Target as Equity Markets Stall $474M Namibia Uranium Build
snippet: Deep Yellow (ASX: DYL) withdrew its Q4 2026 final investment decision target for the Tumas uranium project in Namibia, citing constrained equity market conditions for uranium developers rather than any issue with project economics — civil works continue and are fully funded from existing cash reserves. The deferral marks a setback for a project requiring approximately US$474 million in initial capital; one broker cut its price target to A$1.50 from A$1.95 but kept a speculative buy, viewing the delay as strategic rather than a sign of project distress.

headline: UBS WARNS: Gold Miner Costs to Rise Through 2027 — Buenaventura Cuts Guidance, Sector Margins Under Pressure
snippet: Kitco's Gold SWOT highlights UBS's warning that gold mining companies face sustained operating cost pressures with unit costs likely to rise further into 2027 — even at $4,100+ gold, AISC inflation is eroding expected margin expansion. The report also flags Buenaventura's downward revision to its 2026 gold and silver production guidance, and notes the sector's EV/EBITDA multiple has compressed to 5.7x from a peak of 9.9x in 2014, framing either a historic valuation opportunity or a market correctly pricing structural cost risk.

headline: THE BUYOUT GAP: Junior Gold Developers Priced at $22-71/oz — M&A Benchmarks Show $500-600/oz at $4,000 Gold
snippet: A Discovery Alert analysis quantifies the M&A valuation gap for junior gold developers: projects such as Northern Superior are pricing at an implied US$22–71/oz gold in the ground while comparable acquisition benchmarks run US$500–600/oz — a 7-to-27x discount even at $4,000+ spot gold. The gap is attributed to investor fear of dilution, geopolitical risk, and a persistent equity market preference for producing assets over pre-production developers, creating what the report characterises as a structural mispricing that historically precedes a wave of takeover activity.
